messages:
sam: Heads-up — Corp-X reporting intermittent 5xxs and very high p99 on /v1/generate. They provided three request ids and a tiny curl repro. Asking SRE/runtime for pod + node logs and GPU snapshots. Req IDs: r_aa12, r_bb34, r_cc56

nina: Cluster is redwood-dedicated-eu-west-2, namespace corpx-prod. They said failures started around 2026-02-08T14:10:00Z.

sam: Heres the anonymized curl they ran:
```
curl -X POST https://api.redwood.example/v1/generate \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer sk-corpX" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{"model":"rw-large-v1","input":"summarize: long doc...","max_tokens":512}'
```

ops: Copy. I'll collect: app=inference pod logs, kubelet logs, node syslog, dmesg, and nvidia-smi traces for the 14:00-14:20 window. Starting a debug bundle collector now.

maria: Quick commands to run in the namespace:
```
kubectl -n corpx-prod get pods -l app=inference -o wide
kubectl -n corpx-prod logs -l app=inference --since=2h > /tmp/corpx_pods.log
kubectl -n corpx-prod describe pods -l app=inference > /tmp/corpx_pod_describe.txt
```
On the node (node-21) run: 
```
ssh node-21 sudo dmesg | tail -n 200 > /tmp/node_dmesg.txt
nvidia-smi --query-gpu=index,name,memory.total,memory.used,utilization.gpu,temperature.gpu --format=csv -l 5 --duration=30 > /tmp/gpu_samples.csv
```

runtime-bot: Debug bundle created: bundle_id=dbg-20260208-2134, url=https://ops.redwood/internal/debug/dbg-20260208-2134 (expires in 7d)

ops: Pulled the pod logs around the three request ids. I'm seeing repeated "kv_cache: miss" and then "loading shard" messages followed by a spike in model load activity. Snippet: 
```
[2026-02-08T14:11:23Z] r_bb34 INFO kv_cache: miss for rw-large-v1 shard-2
[2026-02-08T14:11:23Z] r_bb34 INFO model: start async load rw-large-v1@v3
[2026-02-08T14:11:24Z] r_bb34 WARN runtime: tail latency high, seq_len=900
```

maria: Prom metrics for node-21 (14:00-14:20): GPU0 memory climbed to ~15.6GB on a 16GB card, host swap activity spiked, and pod restart_count jumped. Graph links posted in bundle.

alex: Kernel logs show OOM killer activity at 14:11:24: 
```
Feb  8 14:11:24 node-21 kernel: Out of memory: Killed process 45120 (python) total-vm:4800000kB, anon-rss:3800000kB
```
Also dmesg includes GPU resets around the same timestamp.

sam: That timeline aligns with the customer's failure window. Hypothesis: new rw-large-v1@v3 placement or shard density pushed a single GPU over memory, causing OOM -> pod restarts -> cold loads -> repeated memory pressure. Mitigation options: pin customers to rw-large-v1@v2, increase shard spread, or reduce model memory footprint (quantize).

ops: Bundle upload complete: https://ops.redwood/internal/debug/dbg-20260208-2134. Contents: full pod logs, /var/log/kubelet.log, node dmesg/syslog, nvidia-smi CSVs, pod describes, and a short README with timeline and notable lines.

runtime-bot: Created follow-up ticket RUNTIME-7719 for placement investigation. Assignees: alex, ops.

sam: For reproduction, can we ask the customer to run a low-QPS concurrency ramp to capture fresh request ids? Suggest: 
```
for i in $(seq 1 30); do
  curl -s -X POST https://api.redwood.example/v1/generate -H "Authorization: Bearer sk-corpX" -H "Content-Type: application/json" -d '{"model":"rw-large-v1","input":"test","max_tokens":64}' &
  sleep 0.4
done
```
and return any request ids that 5xx. That will help reproduce cache misses vs steady-state behavior.

maria: Also capture response headers (x-request-id, x-runtime-node) so we can map back to specific pods/nodes.

alex: I'll start a GPU memory trace and heap profile on a repro node today and post findings. If we confirm shard packing imbalance we'll propose an autoscaler change to consider model memory when placing shards.

sam: I'll reply to the customer with the debug bundle link, suggested repro script, and temporary mitigation (pin to v2). Closing this support thread for now; will re-open when we have a repro from the customer or a runtime root cause update. :thumbsup:
